verdict.rationale: Slate is a coding agent, and its quickstart shows it being asked to review the architecture of an entire codebase and write an ARCH.md. It also ships a built-in `deep-research` program for researching a problem in parallel, so codebase exploration is plausibly a documented use. However, there is no dedicated doc on codebase mapping or locating change entry points, and the architecture prompt is only an example. missing for 10: dedicated documentation of codebase-understanding features (structure mapping, dependency tracing, identifying where to start changes), and independent or hands-on corroboration that architecture review works well.

support.subject: As a developer, I can understand how a codebase fits together to find where to start making changes

citations.quote: Have slate in parallel deeply research your problem
Please review the architecture of my entire codebase creating an ARCH.md
